examples.trans: The parents ban screens at the table during the evening meal.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Il est strictement interdit de nourrir les canards avec du pain dans ce parc.
examples.trans: It is strictly forbidden to feed the ducks bread in this park.

examples.text: Attention, tu t'engages dans un sens interdit, tourne vite à droite!
examples.trans: Watch out, you're turning down a one-way street the wrong way, turn right quickly!

meanings.en: Interflora, an international network of florists offering flower delivery services
meanings.note: Used invariantly as a proper commercial name in French (envoyer des fleurs par Interflora).

examples.text: J'ai commandé un bouquet de roses par Interflora pour ma mère.
examples.trans: I ordered a bouquet of roses through Interflora for my mother.

examples.text: Ce fleuriste du quartier fait aussi les livraisons Interflora.
examples.trans: This neighborhood florist also handles Interflora deliveries.

meanings.note: Aucune interférence. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'meddling, interference'.

examples.text: Éloigne ton téléphone de la vieille radio, ça provoque des interférences.
examples.trans: Move your phone away from the old radio, it causes interference.

examples.text: J'entends mal ce que tu dis à cause d'une interférence sur la ligne.
examples.trans: I can barely hear what you're saying because of interference on the line.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Nous devons arriver deux heures à l'avance au terminal des vols internationaux.
examples.trans: We need to arrive two hours early at the international flights terminal.

examples.text: Mon cousin travaille dans une entreprise internationale et parle trois langues tous les jours.
examples.trans: My cousin works at an international company and speaks three languages every day.

meanings.note: Sur internet = on the internet. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'internet, online network'.

examples.text: J'ai comparé les prix des hôtels sur internet avant de réserver notre chambre.
examples.trans: I compared hotel prices online before booking our room.

examples.text: La connexion internet ne marche plus depuis l'orage d'hier soir.
examples.trans: The internet connection hasn't been working since last night's storm.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('l'interphone', plural 'les interphones').

examples.text: Le livreur vient de sonner à l'interphone, tu peux lui ouvrir la porte?
examples.trans: The delivery driver just buzzed the intercom, can you open the door for him?

examples.text: L'interphone de l'immeuble est en panne, appelle-moi quand tu es en bas!
examples.trans: The building's intercom is broken, call me when you're downstairs!

meanings.note: Conjugated like rompre (3rd sg il interrompt with -t).

examples.text: L'orage d'été a interrompu le concert dans la cour.
examples.trans: The summer storm interrupted the concert in the courtyard.

examples.text: Excusez-moi de vous interrompre une seconde.
examples.trans: Excuse me for interrupting you for a second.

meanings.note: Appuyer sur l'interrupteur means 'to press/flip the light switch'.

examples.text: L'interrupteur du couloir se trouve à droite de la porte.
examples.trans: The hallway light switch is to the right of the door.

examples.text: Henri remplace le vieil interrupteur par une plaque en laiton.
examples.trans: Henri replaces the old switch with a brass plate.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('l'interruption', plural 'les interruptions').

examples.text: En raison de travaux, il y a une interruption du trafic sur la ligne deux du métro.
examples.trans: Due to construction, there is a service suspension on subway line two.

examples.text: Il a plu sans interruption du matin jusqu'au soir pendant tout le week-end.
examples.trans: It rained nonstop from morning till night all weekend long.

meanings.note: Uses être in compound past tenses: elle est intervenue.

examples.text: Réglez ça ou j'interviens!
examples.trans: Sort it out or I'll step in!

examples.text: La police intervient.
examples.trans: The police step in.

examples.text: Réglez ça en vingt-quatre heures ou j'interviens!
examples.trans: Sort it out in twenty-four hours or I step in!

meanings.note: Usually feminine in French. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard feminine noun meaning 'interview, press interview'.

examples.text: J'ai lu une interview passionnante de cet écrivain dans le journal de dimanche.
examples.trans: I read a fascinating interview with that writer in Sunday's newspaper.

examples.text: Le boulanger qui a gagné le prix de la meilleure baguette donne une interview à la radio locale.
examples.trans: The baker who won the prize for best baguette is giving an interview on local radio.

meanings.note: La pièce la plus intime. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: On a passé une soirée très intime avec quelques vieux amis.
examples.trans: We spent a very intimate evening with a few old friends.

examples.text: Elle écrit tous ses souvenirs dans un petit journal intime.
examples.trans: She writes all her memories in a little diary.

meanings.note: Intimider quelqu'un. Regular -er verb; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'intimidé').

examples.text: Mon nouveau chef m'intimide un peu quand il fronce les sourcils.
examples.trans: My new boss intimidates me a little when he frowns.

examples.text: Ne te laisse pas intimider par ce gros chien, il est très doux!
examples.trans: Don't let yourself be intimidated by that big dog, he is very gentle!

meanings.note: A close private connection, or privacy, depending on context.

examples.text: J'ai besoin d'un peu d'intimité pour passer cet appel téléphonique.
examples.trans: I need a little privacy to make this phone call.

examples.text: Ces rideaux épais protègent bien notre intimité le soir.
examples.trans: These thick curtains protect our privacy well in the evening.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: J'ai lu un article très intéressant dans le journal ce matin.
examples.trans: I read a very interesting article in the newspaper this morning.

examples.text: Cette visite du vieux quartier de Lyon était vraiment intéressante!
examples.trans: That tour of the old district of Lyon was really interesting!

meanings.note: Ça m'intéresse = that interests me.

meanings.en: s'intéresser à = to be interested in

examples.text: C'est ce qui m'intéresse.
examples.trans: That's what interests me.

examples.text: Ce rôle m'intéresse beaucoup.
examples.trans: This part interests me a lot.

meanings.note: Intéressé par = interested in.

examples.text: Tu es intéressé par ce vieux vélo ou je le vends?
examples.trans: Are you interested in this old bike or shall I sell it?

examples.text: Ma sœur est très intéressée par l'annonce pour cet appartement.
examples.trans: My sister is very interested in the ad for this apartment.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('l'intérieur', plural 'les intérieurs').

examples.text: La scène suivante est tournée à l'intérieur du château.
examples.trans: The next scene is filmed inside the castle.

examples.text: Elle cache une grande force à l'intérieur.
examples.trans: She hides a great strength on the inside.

meanings.note: Par intérim = acting, interim. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'interim, temporary work'.

examples.text: Mon frère travaille en intérim dans une boulangerie cet été.
examples.trans: My brother is doing temp work in a bakery this summer.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé une mission d'intérim de trois semaines au bureau.
examples.trans: I found a three-week temp assignment at the office.

meanings.note: Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Standard masculine noun meaning 'interest, self-interest'.

examples.text: Tu as tout intérêt à réserver ton billet de train tôt.
examples.trans: It is in your best interest to book your train ticket early.

examples.text: Elle écoute avec beaucoup d'intérêt les conseils du vieux jardinier.
examples.trans: She listens with great interest to the old gardener's advice.

meanings.note: Un exercice inutile. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion.

examples.text: C'est inutile de courir, le train vient déjà de partir.
examples.trans: It's pointless to run, the train has just left.

examples.text: J'ai jeté plein d'objets inutiles en rangeant le garage dimanche.
examples.trans: I threw away lots of useless things while tidying the garage on Sunday.

meanings.en: to make up a story, invent

examples.text: Arrête d'inventer des excuses parce que tu es en retard!
examples.trans: Stop making up excuses because you're late!

examples.text: Mon père adore inventer des histoires drôles pour endormir les enfants.
examples.trans: My father loves making up funny stories to put the children to sleep.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('l'inverse', plural 'les inverses').

examples.text: Tu préfères le thé froid? Moi, c'est tout l'inverse!
examples.trans: Do you prefer cold tea? For me, it's quite the opposite!

examples.text: Prends la rue dans le sens inverse pour rejoindre la gare.
examples.trans: Take the street in the opposite direction to get to the train station.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to reverse'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'inversé').

examples.text: Pardon, le serveur a inversé nos deux assiettes par erreur.
examples.trans: Excuse me, the waiter switched our two plates by mistake.

examples.text: On peut inverser nos jours de congé la semaine prochaine?
examples.trans: Can we swap our days off next week?

meanings.note: French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Core French verb meaning 'to invest'.

examples.text: Mes parents veulent investir leurs économies dans un petit appartement.
examples.trans: My parents want to invest their savings in a small apartment.

examples.text: On a décidé d'investir dans un bon matelas pour mieux dormir.
examples.trans: We decided to invest in a good mattress to sleep better.

meanings.note: perdre son investissement = to lose one's investment

examples.text: Un bon manteau d'hiver, c'est un excellent investissement pour des années.
examples.trans: A good winter coat is an excellent investment for years.

examples.text: L'achat de cette petite boutique demande un gros investissement au départ.
examples.trans: Buying this small shop requires a big investment at first.

meanings.note: Something that cannot be seen; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: La tache sur ta chemise est presque invisible maintenant.
examples.trans: The stain on your shirt is almost invisible now.

examples.text: Avec ce brouillard épais, le bout de la rue est complètement invisible.
examples.trans: With this thick fog, the end of the street is completely invisible.

meanings.note: une invitation à / aux = an invitation to

examples.text: Nous avons reçu une jolie invitation pour son repas d'anniversaire.
examples.trans: We received a lovely invitation to her birthday meal.

examples.text: J'accepte votre aimable invitation à boire un café avec plaisir.
examples.trans: I gladly accept your kind invitation to have a coffee.

meanings.note: Inviter quelqu'un à prendre le thé = invite someone for tea.

examples.text: Nous avons invité tous les voisins de la rue vendredi.
examples.trans: We invited all the neighbors on the street on Friday.

examples.text: Je vous invite à boire une tasse de thé chaud.
examples.trans: I invite you to have a cup of hot tea.

meanings.en: guest (at an event, dinner, or gathering)
meanings.note: Feminine form: une invitée.

examples.text: Chaque invité trouve une chaise autour des tables.
examples.trans: Every guest finds a chair around the tables.

examples.text: Allons accueillir notre première invitée au portail!
examples.trans: Let's go welcome our first guest at the gate!

meanings.en: unpublished, never before performed or released
meanings.note: Une valse inédite = an unpublished waltz.

examples.text: Elle a retrouvé une partition inédite dans le pupitre.
examples.trans: She found an unpublished score inside the music stand.

examples.text: Ce carnet contient trois poèmes inédits.
examples.trans: This notebook contains three unpublished poems.

meanings.en: Ireland, an island in northwestern Europe and the sovereign Republic of Ireland
meanings.note: Feminine singular country name starting with a vowel in French: l'Irlande (en Irlande, venir d'Irlande).

examples.text: Il pleut souvent en Irlande, mais les paysages sont magnifiques!
examples.trans: It often rains in Ireland, but the landscapes are magnificent!

examples.text: Mon cousin prend le ferry à Cherbourg pour aller en Irlande.
examples.trans: My cousin is taking the ferry in Cherbourg to go to Ireland.

meanings.note: une situation irrattrapable = an unrecoverable situation

examples.text: J'ai mis trop de sel dans la soupe, elle est irrattrapable!
examples.trans: I put too much salt in the soup, it's beyond saving!

examples.text: Après une heure d'embouteillage, notre retard était devenu irrattrapable.
examples.trans: After an hour in a traffic jam, our delay had become unrecoverable.

meanings.note: Adjective of capability/quality formed with '-able'/'-ible' (from Latin '-abilis'/'-ibilis').

examples.text: Notre vieille boulangère prend sa retraite demain, elle est vraiment irremplaçable.
examples.trans: Our old baker is retiring tomorrow, she is truly irreplaceable.

examples.text: Fais attention à cette tasse ancienne, elle est irremplaçable pour ma mère.
examples.trans: Be careful with this antique cup, it is irreplaceable to my mother.

meanings.note: Not acting with proper care or responsibility; same singular spelling for masculine and feminine.

examples.text: C'est irresponsable de conduire aussi vite sous la pluie!
examples.trans: It's irresponsible to drive that fast in the rain!

examples.text: Laisser un chien seul au soleil dans la voiture, c'est complètement irresponsable.
examples.trans: Leaving a dog alone in the sun in the car is completely irresponsible.

meanings.en: Isabelle, a classic French female given name equivalent to English Isabel or Isabella
meanings.note: Also gave rise in French to a lower-case color adjective isabelle ('isabelline, pale cream-fawn'), named after royal figures bearing the given name.

examples.text: Isabelle choisit des pommes et des poires au marché.
examples.trans: Isabelle is choosing apples and pears at the market.

examples.text: À quelle heure est-ce qu'Isabelle rentre du travail ce soir?
examples.trans: What time does Isabelle get home from work tonight?

meanings.note: Du ruban isolant (or du chatterton) is insulating electrical tape.

examples.text: Henri entoure la connexion proprement avec du ruban isolant noir.
examples.trans: Henri wraps the connection neatly with black electrical tape.

examples.text: Ce rideau épais est aussi très isolant contre le froid.
examples.trans: This thick curtain also insulates very well against the cold.

examples.text: C'est l'isolement qui m'intéresse.
examples.trans: It's the isolation that interests me.

examples.text: Il vit dans l'isolement.
examples.trans: He lives in isolation.

meanings.note: Planned path or sequence of stops from one place to another.

examples.text: Nous avons tracé tout l'itinéraire au crayon sur le plan.
examples.trans: We traced the whole route in pencil on the map.

examples.text: Cet itinéraire passe par les plus jolies ruelles de la ville.
examples.trans: This route goes through the prettiest lanes in town.

meanings.note: Masculine noun: des touches en ivoire ('ivory piano keys'). Also used invariable as an off-white colour shade.

examples.text: Ce piano ancien a encore ses touches en ivoire d'origine.
examples.trans: This antique piano still has its original ivory keys.

examples.text: La lumière donne au mur une belle teinte ivoire.
examples.trans: The light gives the wall a lovely ivory tint.

meanings.note: Être ivre = to be drunk. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'drunk'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Après trois verres de vin, il était un peu ivre.
examples.trans: After three glasses of wine, he was a little drunk.

examples.text: Un homme ivre chantait très fort dans la rue hier soir.
examples.trans: A drunk man was singing very loudly in the street last night.

meanings.en: Jacques, a classic French male given name corresponding historically to James and Jacob
meanings.note: The final -s is silent in isolation and stems from the Old French masculine nominative case ending; the -c- was added in Middle French spelling.

examples.text: Jacques lit le journal sur la terrasse du café.
examples.trans: Jacques is reading the newspaper on the café terrace.

examples.text: Peux-tu passer le sel à Jacques, s'il te plaît?
examples.trans: Can you pass the salt to Jacques, please?

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'formerly'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Jadis, il y avait un joli moulin au bord de cette rivière.
examples.trans: In former times, there was a pretty mill by this river.

examples.text: Mon grand-père raconte souvent comment on vivait jadis au village.
examples.trans: My grandfather often tells how people used to live in the village.

meanings.en: Jafar, a male given name of Arabic and Persian usage meaning 'brook' or 'rivulet'
meanings.note: Commonly pronounced in French with an initial affricate (as in Persian and Arabic dialects with affricated jīm), though some speakers adapt initial j- to a native French postalveolar fricative.

examples.text: Jafar ouvre sa boulangerie tous les jours à six heures.
examples.trans: Jafar opens his bakery every day at six o'clock.

examples.text: Tu as le numéro de téléphone de Jafar?
examples.trans: Do you have Jafar's phone number?

meanings.note: La jalousie est stupide. Feminine noun ('la jalousie', plural 'les jalousies').

examples.text: Sa jalousie devient fatigante dès que je parle à mes collègues.
examples.trans: His jealousy gets tiring whenever I talk to my colleagues.

examples.text: Il n'y a aucune jalousie entre ma sœur et moi.
examples.trans: There is no jealousy at all between my sister and me.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'jealous'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le chat est jaloux quand on caresse le chien du voisin.
examples.trans: The cat is jealous when we pet the neighbor's dog.

examples.text: Ma petite sœur est un peu jalouse de mon vélo neuf.
examples.trans: My little sister is a bit jealous of my new bike.

meanings.note: With ne: je ne mens jamais.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu un acteur aussi exigeant!
examples.trans: I have never seen such a demanding actor!

examples.text: Il ne répond jamais au téléphone pendant le week-end.
examples.trans: He never answers the phone during the weekend.

examples.text: Oh... oh non. Où est ma chaise? J'ai les jambes qui tremblent.
examples.trans: Oh... oh no. Where is my chair? My legs are shaking.

examples.text: J'ai mal aux jambes.
examples.trans: My legs hurt.

meanings.en: James, an English male given name also used in France and the francophone world
meanings.note: Pronounced in modern French with an English-adapted affricate initial and sounded final -s (unlike older regional French surname pronunciations with native j-).

examples.text: James apprend le français depuis six mois à Lyon.
examples.trans: James has been learning French for six months in Lyon.

examples.text: Est-ce que le sac à dos bleu appartient à James?
examples.trans: Does the blue backpack belong to James?

meanings.en: Janowski, a surname of Polish toponymic origin
meanings.note: In everyday French, initial J- is commonly adapted to the French postalveolar fricative (or kept as a palatal glide closer to Polish), and -w- before voiceless -sk- is pronounced -f-.

examples.text: Monsieur Janowski prend le métro tous les matins à huit heures.
examples.trans: Mr. Janowski takes the subway every morning at eight o'clock.

examples.text: Voici la facture pour Madame Janowski, merci beaucoup!
examples.trans: Here is the invoice for Mrs. Janowski, thank you very much!

meanings.note: Courtyard or backyard garden.

examples.text: Bon endroit. Deux chaises solides, tournées vers les herbes du jardin et pas vers la fenêtre.
examples.trans: Good spot. Two solid chairs, facing the garden herbs and not the window.

examples.text: Ma mère plante des tomates et des fraises dans son jardin.
examples.trans: My mother plants tomatoes and strawberries in her garden.

examples.text: Je jardine le dimanche.
examples.trans: I garden on Sundays.

examples.text: Elle aime jardiner.
examples.trans: She likes gardening.

meanings.note: Used as a French surname of regional occupational or topographic origin.

examples.text: Monsieur Jarron attend son train sur le quai.
examples.trans: Mr. Jarron is waiting for his train on the platform.

examples.text: La boulangerie de la famille Jarron ouvre à sept heures.
examples.trans: The Jarron family's bakery opens at seven o'clock.

meanings.note: same form in masculine and feminine

examples.text: Elle porte une écharpe jaune très chaude pour sortir cet hiver.
examples.trans: She wears a very warm yellow scarf to go out this winter.

examples.text: Les citrons jaunes du marché sont parfaits pour faire une tarte.
examples.trans: The yellow lemons from the market are perfect for making a tart.

meanings.note: Un club de jazz. Masculine noun ('le jazz', plural 'les —').

examples.text: Mon père écoute toujours du jazz en préparant le dîner.
examples.trans: My father always listens to jazz while making dinner.

examples.text: Il y a un petit concert de jazz gratuit au parc ce soir.
examples.trans: There is a free little jazz concert in the park tonight.

meanings.note: J' before a vowel.

examples.text: Je n'ai jamais vu cette boîte en quinze ans!
examples.trans: I have never seen that box in fifteen years!

examples.text: Je prends toujours un croissant chaud à la boulangerie le dimanche.
examples.trans: I always get a warm croissant at the bakery on Sundays.

meanings.en: Jean (a masculine given name, cognate with English John)
meanings.note: Classic French masculine given name, occurring both standalone and as the first element of many hyphenated compound names.

examples.text: Jean achète du pain frais tous les matins.
examples.trans: Jean buys fresh bread every morning.

examples.text: Tu sais à quelle heure Jean rentre du bureau?
examples.trans: Do you know what time Jean gets home from the office?

meanings.en: Jean-Denis (a French compound masculine given name)
meanings.note: French masculine *prénom composé* uniting *Jean* and *Denis* (historically associated in France with Saint Denis of Paris).

examples.text: Jean-Denis travaille dans une banque près de la gare.
examples.trans: Jean-Denis works in a bank near the train station.

examples.text: J'ai laissé les clés de la voiture à Jean-Denis.
examples.trans: I left the car keys with Jean-Denis.

meanings.en: Jean-Jacques (a French compound masculine given name)
meanings.note: One of the best-known traditional French compound masculine names, popularized since the eighteenth century.

examples.text: Jean-Jacques prend toujours un café noir après le déjeuner.
examples.trans: Jean-Jacques always has a black coffee after lunch.

examples.text: Est-ce que Jean-Jacques vient dîner chez nous samedi?
examples.trans: Is Jean-Jacques coming to have dinner at our place on Saturday?

meanings.en: Jean-Louis (a French compound masculine given name)
meanings.note: Traditional French *prénom composé* pairing biblical *Jean* with royal Frankish *Louis*.

examples.text: Jean-Louis répare son vélo dans le jardin.
examples.trans: Jean-Louis is fixing his bicycle in the garden.

examples.text: Nous avons rendez-vous avec Jean-Louis devant la mairie.
examples.trans: We have an appointment with Jean-Louis in front of town hall.

meanings.note: jeter un coup d'œil = to have a look / glance

examples.text: Je vais jeter un coup d'œil dans le sac.
examples.trans: I'm going to take a look inside the bag.

examples.text: Ne jette rien par terre.
examples.trans: Don't throw anything on the ground.

examples.text: jeter un coup d'œil
examples.trans: to take a quick look

meanings.note: Game or pastime ('jeu de piste' = treasure/scavenger hunt); set of cards or keys.

examples.text: Toute la matinée ressemble à un grand jeu de piste.
examples.trans: The whole morning feels like a grand treasure hunt.

examples.text: Il garde un second jeu de clés derrière le comptoir.
examples.trans: He keeps a spare set of keys behind the counter.

examples.text: Le marché est ouvert le jeudi matin.
examples.trans: The market is open on Thursday mornings.

examples.text: Jeudi, on répare enfin la chaudière.
examples.trans: On Thursday we finally fix the boiler.

meanings.note: Goes before the noun.

examples.text: C'est une jeune femme.
examples.trans: She's a young woman.

examples.text: Le jeune serveur du café est toujours souriant avec les clients.
examples.trans: The young waiter at the café is always smiling with the customers.

meanings.note: La jeunesse = youth / youthfulness. Feminine noun ('la jeunesse', plural 'les jeunesses').

examples.text: Mon grand-père raconte souvent des souvenirs joyeux de sa jeunesse.
examples.trans: My grandfather often tells happy memories from his youth.

examples.text: Elle a passé toute sa jeunesse dans un petit village calme.
examples.trans: She spent her whole youth in a quiet little village.

meanings.en: Games (capitalized proper name for major athletic competitions, especially the Olympic Games)
meanings.note: Capitalized in French when used elliptically as a proper noun (*les Jeux*) referring to the Olympic Games or similar official multi-sport events.

examples.text: Toute la ville prépare l'accueil des Jeux cet été.
examples.trans: The whole city is preparing to host the Games this summer.

examples.text: Nous regardons la cérémonie d'ouverture des Jeux à la télévision.
examples.trans: We are watching the opening ceremony of the Games on television.

meanings.en: Joey (a masculine given name or diminutive of Joseph)
meanings.note: English diminutive given name used in French both as an independent first name and as a short form.

examples.text: Joey habite au troisième étage de notre immeuble.
examples.trans: Joey lives on the third floor of our building.

examples.text: Tu peux appeler Joey avant de partir à la gare?
examples.trans: Can you call Joey before leaving for the station?

meanings.note: Compound stage name formed from English *Joey* and *Starr* (stylized spelling of *star*).

examples.text: Mon frère écoute un vieil album de JoeyStarr dans le salon.
examples.trans: My brother is listening to an old JoeyStarr album in the living room.

examples.text: J'ai trouvé ce disque de JoeyStarr au marché aux puces.
examples.trans: I found this JoeyStarr record at the flea market.

meanings.note: Swedish patronymic surname meaning "son of Johan", corresponding in etymology to English *Johnson*.

examples.text: Madame Johansson a réservé une chambre calme à l'hôtel.
examples.trans: Mrs. Johansson booked a quiet room at the hotel.

examples.text: Le colis pour la famille Johansson est arrivé ce matin.
examples.trans: The package for the Johansson family arrived this morning.

meanings.en: John (an English masculine given name, cognate with French Jean)
meanings.note: English masculine given name frequently encountered in French, cognate with native *Jean*.

examples.text: John apprend le français dans une école de langues.
examples.trans: John is learning French at a language school.

examples.text: Nous prenons le train de huit heures avec John.
examples.trans: We are taking the eight o'clock train with John.

meanings.note: A feeling of happiness; plein de joie, full of joy.

examples.text: Quelle joie!
examples.trans: What joy!

examples.text: Elle est pleine de joie.
examples.trans: She's full of joy.

joindre.gloss: to join, to reach, to contact

meanings.en: to reach, to contact; to join, to attach
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to join, to reach, to contact'.

examples.text: J'essaie de joindre le plombier depuis ce matin, mais ça ne répond pas.
examples.trans: I've been trying to reach the plumber since this morning, but there's no answer.

examples.text: N'oublie pas de joindre une photo à ton dossier d'inscription.
examples.trans: Don't forget to attach a photo to your registration file.

meanings.note: Plumbing joint between two pipes.

examples.text: Tenez cette lampe de poche bien droite sur le joint du tuyau, juste ici.
examples.trans: Hold this flashlight steady on the pipe joint, right here.

examples.text: Le robinet de la cuisine goutte parce que le joint est usé.
examples.trans: The kitchen faucet drips because the gasket is worn out.

examples.text: C'est une jolie robe.
examples.trans: It's a pretty dress.

examples.text: Vous êtes sûre? Il a l'air joli et bien chaud!
examples.trans: Are you sure? It looks lovely and nice and warm!

meanings.en: Jonas (a masculine given name, equivalent to English Jonah or Jonas)
meanings.note: Biblical masculine given name used across French, German, and Scandinavian languages; final *-s* is pronounced in French (/ʒonas/).

examples.text: Jonas prépare une soupe chaude pour ce soir.
examples.trans: Jonas is making hot soup for tonight.

examples.text: J'ai croisé Jonas devant la librairie du quartier.
examples.trans: I ran into Jonas in front of the neighborhood bookstore.

meanings.note: Biblical masculine given name widely adopted in France since the late twentieth century.

examples.text: Jonathan cherche un nouvel appartement près du métro.
examples.trans: Jonathan is looking for a new apartment near the subway.

examples.text: Tu as envoyé le document à Jonathan cet après-midi?
examples.trans: Did you send the document to Jonathan this afternoon?

meanings.en: Jones (a Welsh and English patronymic surname)
meanings.note: Very common Welsh and English surname meaning "son of John".

examples.text: Monsieur Jones prend le petit-déjeuner sur la terrasse du café.
examples.trans: Mr. Jones is having breakfast on the café terrace.

examples.text: La valise de Madame Jones est déjà dans le taxi.
examples.trans: Mrs. Jones's suitcase is already in the taxi.

meanings.en: José (a masculine given name of Spanish and Portuguese origin, cognate with Joseph)
meanings.note: Iberian equivalent of *Joseph*, well established in France with French-adapted pronunciation /ʒoze/.

examples.text: José ouvre sa boutique de fleurs dès huit heures.
examples.trans: José opens his flower shop at eight o'clock sharp.

examples.text: Nous allons boire un thé chez José dimanche après-midi.
examples.trans: We are going to have tea at José's place on Sunday afternoon.

meanings.en: Joubert (a French family name of Germanic origin)
meanings.note: Common French patronymic surname continuing a medieval Germanic given name.

examples.text: Le docteur Joubert reçoit ses patients le mardi matin.
examples.trans: Doctor Joubert sees his patients on Tuesday mornings.

examples.text: J'ai déposé le courrier dans la boîte de la famille Joubert.
examples.trans: I dropped the mail in the Joubert family's mailbox.

examples.text: Elle a des joues roses.
examples.trans: She has pink cheeks.

examples.text: Il faut faire les joues.
examples.trans: The cheeks need doing.

meanings.note: jouer un rôle, jouer le frère de.
Je joue dans un spectacle.
Jouer au foot, jouer du piano.

examples.text: Les enfants jouent au ballon dans le jardin après l'école.
examples.trans: The children play ball in the garden after school.

examples.text: Ma sœur joue très bien du piano dans le salon.
examples.trans: My sister plays the piano very well in the living room.

meanings.en: Chubby-cheeks (a playful descriptive French nickname meaning "plump-cheeked one")
meanings.note: Hyphenated descriptive *sobriquet* built from *joues rebondies* ("plump, chubby cheeks").

examples.text: Le bébé sourit tout le temps, alors sa grand-mère l'appelle Joues-rebondies!
examples.trans: The baby smiles all the time, so his grandmother calls him Chubby-cheeks!

examples.text: Viens goûter ta compote de pommes, petit Joues-rebondies!
examples.trans: Come taste your applesauce, little Chubby-cheeks!

meanings.note: Feminine: joueuse. Derived with the Romance agent/quality suffix '-eur'/'-euse' (from Latin '-or'/'-tor'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'player, gambler'.

examples.text: Mon cousin est le meilleur joueur de son équipe de basket.
examples.trans: My cousin is the best player on his basketball team.

examples.text: Il nous manque un quatrième joueur pour commencer la partie de cartes.
examples.trans: We are missing a fourth player to start the card game.

examples.text: Un jour.
examples.trans: One day.

examples.text: Chaque jour.
examples.trans: Every day.

meanings.en: that very day (used with demonstrative ce: ce jour-là)
meanings.note: Hyphenated -là points back to a specific day in the past or future.

examples.text: Depuis ce jour-là, les deux frères ne s'étaient plus parlé.
examples.trans: Since that day, the two brothers hadn't spoken to each other again.

examples.text: Il pleuvait à verse ce jour-là quand le train est arrivé.
examples.trans: It was pouring rain that day when the train pulled in.

meanings.note: Irregular -al -> -aux plural (les journaux). Du papier journal (no preposition) means 'newspaper / newsprint' used for wrapping fragile goods at market.

examples.text: La marchande emballe chaque assiette dans du papier journal.
examples.trans: The stallholder wraps each plate in newspaper.

examples.text: Odette lit le journal local en buvant son thé.
examples.trans: Odette reads the local newspaper while drinking her tea.

meanings.note: un article de journaliste = a journalist's article

examples.text: Une journaliste locale a posé des questions au maire devant la mairie.
examples.trans: A local journalist asked the mayor questions in front of town hall.

examples.text: Mon voisin est journaliste sportif pour un quotidien de Lyon.
examples.trans: My neighbor is a sports journalist for a daily newspaper in Lyon.

meanings.note: the whole day, as time you live through; bonne journée = have a nice day

examples.text: Quelle longue journée à l'hôtel!
examples.trans: What a long day at the hotel!

examples.text: Bonne journée et à ce soir pour le dîner!
examples.trans: Have a nice day and see you tonight for dinner!

meanings.note: Plural in -x: joyaux. Masculine noun ('le joyau', plural 'les joyaux').

examples.text: Ce petit village au bord de l'eau est un vrai joyau.
examples.trans: This little village by the water is a real gem.

examples.text: On a admiré les joyaux anciens exposés au musée dimanche après-midi.
examples.trans: We admired the antique jewels on display at the museum on Sunday afternoon.

meanings.en: Juan (a Spanish masculine given name, cognate with Jean and John)
meanings.note: Spanish form of *John*/*Jean*; in French, speakers usually approximate Spanish /xwan/ (except in the fixed literary compound *Don Juan*, traditionally gallicized as /dɔ̃ʒɥɑ̃/).

examples.text: Juan prépare une paella pour toute sa famille dimanche.
examples.trans: Juan is making a paella for his whole family on Sunday.

examples.text: J'ai rencontré Juan dans le train entre Madrid et Bordeaux.
examples.trans: I met Juan on the train between Madrid and Bordeaux.

meanings.en: Judas (a biblical proper name; by extension, a traitor or betrayer)
meanings.note: Used in French as the biblical proper name and figuratively by antonomasia (*un Judas*) for someone who betrays a friend's trust.

examples.text: Ce vieux tableau à l'église représente le baiser de Judas.
examples.trans: This old painting in the church depicts the kiss of Judas.

examples.text: Ne fais pas confiance à cet homme déloyal, c'est un vrai Judas!
examples.trans: Don't trust that disloyal man, he's a real Judas!

meanings.note: Le professeur de judo. Masculine noun ('le judo', plural 'les judos').

examples.text: Ma nièce fait du judo tous les mercredis après-midi au gymnase.
examples.trans: My niece does judo every Wednesday afternoon at the gym.

examples.text: Mon fils vient d'obtenir sa ceinture orange au club de judo.
examples.trans: My son just got his orange belt at the judo club.

related.gloss: a judo martial art / judo martial arts

meanings.note: Also feminine: une juge. Masculine noun ('le juge', plural 'les juges').

examples.text: Le juge va décider.
examples.trans: The judge will decide.

examples.text: La juge a écouté calmement les deux voisins avant de répondre.
examples.trans: The judge listened calmly to both neighbors before answering.

meanings.note: Masculine action/result noun formed with the Romance suffix '-ment' (from Latin '-mentum'). Standard masculine noun meaning 'opinion, appraisal, judgment'.

examples.text: Ne porte pas de jugement trop rapide sans connaître toute l'histoire.
examples.trans: Don't make too quick a judgment without knowing the whole story.

examples.text: Je fais entièrement confiance au jugement de mon médecin de famille.
examples.trans: I completely trust the judgment of my family doctor.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to judge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'jugé').

examples.text: Il ne faut pas juger un plat avant de goûter.
examples.trans: You shouldn't judge a dish before tasting it.

examples.text: Le boulanger juge que la pâte à pain est enfin prête.
examples.trans: The baker judges that the bread dough is finally ready.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le juin', plural 'les juins').

examples.text: Les jours sont très longs et agréables au mois de juin.
examples.trans: The days are very long and pleasant in the month of June.

examples.text: L'école finit fin juin et les enfants ont déjà hâte!
examples.trans: School ends in late June and the kids can hardly wait already!

meanings.en: Juju (an affectionate French nickname for names like Julie, Julien, or Juliette)
meanings.note: Informal gender-neutral French pet name created by reduplicating the opening syllable /ʒy/.

examples.text: Bon anniversaire Juju, j'ai acheté ton gâteau préféré!
examples.trans: Happy birthday Juju, I bought your favorite cake!

examples.text: Dépêche-toi Juju, le bus va partir dans deux minutes!
examples.trans: Hurry up Juju, the bus is going to leave in two minutes!

meanings.en: Julie (a feminine given name, cognate with Julia)
meanings.note: Classic French feminine given name corresponding to Latin and English *Julia*.

examples.text: Julie boit un chocolat chaud près de la fenêtre.
examples.trans: Julie is drinking a hot chocolate near the window.

examples.text: Est-ce que Julie travaille à la bibliothèque aujourd'hui?
examples.trans: Is Julie working at the library today?

meanings.en: Julien, a French masculine given name corresponding to English Julian, also occurring as a French surname.
meanings.note: Widely borne across the Francophone world since the Middle Ages due to the veneration of Saint Julian the Hospitaller and Saint Julian of Brioude.

examples.text: Julien achète du pain frais à la boulangerie.
examples.trans: Julien buys fresh bread at the bakery.

examples.text: Tu viens prendre un café avec Julien ce matin?
examples.trans: Are you coming to have a coffee with Julien this morning?

meanings.en: Juliette, a French feminine given name corresponding to English Juliet.
meanings.note: Originally an affectionate diminutive of Julie that became established as an independent given name throughout French-speaking regions.

examples.text: Juliette attend le train sur le quai numéro trois.
examples.trans: Juliette is waiting for the train on platform number three.

examples.text: J'ai réservé une table au restaurant pour Juliette.
examples.trans: I booked a table at the restaurant for Juliette.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'twin'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Il ressemble beaucoup à son frère jumeau.
examples.trans: He looks a lot like his twin brother.

examples.text: Les deux sœurs jumelles travaillent dans le cinéma.
examples.trans: The two twin sisters work in cinema.

meanings.note: Un agent junior. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'junior'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Mon neveu nage dans la catégorie junior au club municipal.
examples.trans: My nephew swims in the junior category at the local club.

examples.text: Ils cherchent un comptable junior pour renforcer l'équipe du bureau.
examples.trans: They are looking for a junior accountant to strengthen the office team.

meanings.note: porter une jupe = to wear a skirt; tout ce qui porte une jupe = anything in a skirt (colloquial for women)

examples.text: Elle a acheté une jolie jupe plissée pour l'été.
examples.trans: She bought a pretty pleated skirt for the summer.

examples.text: Il fait trop froid ce matin pour sortir en jupe sans collants.
examples.trans: It is too cold this morning to go out in a skirt without tights.

meanings.note: An emphatic assurance; it need not refer to a legal oath.
Colours can clash: ces couleurs jurent.

examples.text: Je te jure que j'ai bien fermé la porte à clé!
examples.trans: I swear to you that I locked the door properly!

examples.text: Ces chaussettes oranges jurent vraiment avec ton pantalon bleu marine.
examples.trans: Those orange socks really clash with your navy blue pants.

meanings.note: to do with the law: le service juridique = the Legal Department

examples.text: Voici le service juridique.
examples.trans: This is the Legal Department.

examples.text: C'est un problème juridique.
examples.trans: It's a legal problem.

examples.text: Un jus d'orange.
examples.trans: An orange juice.

examples.text: Permettez-moi de servir le jus d'orange frais, madame!
examples.trans: Allow me to pour the fresh orange juice, madam!

meanings.note: Jusqu'à demain = until tomorrow.

examples.text: J'attends jusqu'à demain.
examples.trans: I'll wait until tomorrow.

examples.text: Il travaille jusqu'à huit heures.
examples.trans: He works until eight.

meanings.note: Elides to jusqu' before vowels: jusqu'à demain, jusqu'au bout.

examples.text: Je lis le mot: Désolé pour l'erreur. Gardez mon sac bleu jusqu'à vendredi, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Let me read the note: Sorry for the mistake. Please keep my blue bag until Friday.

examples.text: Jusqu'à vendredi? Pas de nom, pas de signature!
examples.trans: Until Friday? No name, no signature!

examples.text: Pourquoi laisser ses chaussures et son train en bois chez des inconnus jusqu'à vendredi?
examples.trans: Why leave one's shoes and wooden train with strangers until Friday?

meanings.en: that far, up to that point; until then, so far
meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'that far'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Tout allait très bien jusque-là, puis l'orage a éclaté d'un coup.
examples.trans: Everything was going fine until then, and then the storm broke out all of a sudden.

examples.text: La boulangerie est au bout de l'avenue; tu peux marcher jusque-là?
examples.trans: The bakery is at the end of the avenue; can you walk that far?

meanings.note: Adverb: je veux juste.
Adjective.

examples.text: Juste là sur votre front, bien au chaud.
examples.trans: Right there on your forehead, safe and sound.

examples.text: Sur la cour, juste au-dessus du vieux tilleul. C'est très calme.
examples.trans: The courtyard, right above the old linden tree. It is very quiet.

examples.text: Juste sous cette arche. Je vais monter la valise bleue pour vous.
examples.trans: Right under this archway. I will carry the blue suitcase up for you.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a . mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Je pensais justement à vous.
examples.trans: I was just thinking of you.

examples.text: Oh, mon carnet en cuir! Merci! Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: Oh, my leather notebook! Thank you! I was just looking for it.

examples.text: Je le cherchais justement.
examples.trans: I was just looking for it.

meanings.note: attaquer en justice = to take legal action, to sue

examples.text: Les habitants du quartier demandent simplement un peu plus de justice.
examples.trans: The neighborhood residents are simply asking for a bit more justice.

examples.text: Cette affaire compliquée sera bientôt réglée devant la justice.
examples.trans: This complicated matter will soon be settled in court.

meanings.en: Kadropov, a surname of Russian or Slavic morphological pattern used in French.
meanings.note: Follows the standard French transliteration -ov for masculine Slavic family names ending in Cyrillic -ов.

examples.text: Monsieur Kadropov arrive à l'hôtel vers midi.
examples.trans: Mr. Kadropov arrives at the hotel around noon.

examples.text: Le dossier de Monsieur Kadropov est sur le bureau.
examples.trans: Mr. Kadropov's file is on the desk.

meanings.en: Kahn, a surname common in France (especially Alsace and Lorraine) and German-speaking countries.
meanings.note: Traditionally borne by Ashkenazi families tracing priestly lineage; occasionally conflated in German homonymy with Kahn ('small boat').

examples.text: Monsieur Kahn travaille dans cette banque depuis dix ans.
examples.trans: Mr. Kahn has worked in this bank for ten years.

examples.text: Avez-vous envoyé le courrier à Madame Kahn?
examples.trans: Did you send the mail to Mrs. Kahn?

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le karma', plural 'les karmas').

examples.text: J'ai rendu un portefeuille perdu et j'ai gagné au loto: c'est le karma!
examples.trans: I returned a lost wallet and won the lottery: that's karma!

examples.text: Sois gentil avec tes voisins, c'est bon pour ton karma.
examples.trans: Be nice to your neighbors, it's good for your karma.

meanings.en: Kechiche, a family name of Tunisian and Maghrebi Arabic origin attested in France and North Africa.
meanings.note: Transcribed according to standard French conventions for Maghrebi Arabic, where ch represents the postalveolar fricative [ʃ].

examples.text: Monsieur Kechiche prend le train de huit heures pour aller au bureau.
examples.trans: Mr. Kechiche takes the eight o'clock train to go to the office.

examples.text: La boulangerie à côté de chez Madame Kechiche ouvre tôt.
examples.trans: The bakery next to Mrs. Kechiche's place opens early.

meanings.en: Kerr, a surname of Scottish and northern English origin encountered in French and international contexts.
meanings.note: Originally denoted someone who lived near a marshy copse in northern Britain; closely related to the English variant Carr.

examples.text: Madame Kerr cherche la sortie de la gare centrale.
examples.trans: Mrs. Kerr is looking for the exit of the central train station.

examples.text: Nous avons rendez-vous avec Monsieur Kerr cet après-midi.
examples.trans: We have an appointment with Mr. Kerr this afternoon.

meanings.en: Kiberlain, a French surname adapted from an Eastern European Ashkenazi family name.
meanings.note: The French spelling -ain naturally yields the nasal vowel [ɛ̃] in spoken French.

examples.text: Madame Kiberlain habite au troisième étage de cet immeuble.
examples.trans: Mrs. Kiberlain lives on the third floor of this building.

examples.text: J'ai laissé un message pour Monsieur Kiberlain à la réception.
examples.trans: I left a message for Mr. Kiberlain at the front desk.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to enjoy'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'kiffé').

examples.text: Mes cousins ont vraiment kiffé leurs vacances au bord de la mer.
examples.trans: My cousins really loved their vacation by the sea.

examples.text: Je kiffe trop la nouvelle pizzeria au coin de notre rue!
examples.trans: I totally love the new pizzeria on the corner of our street!

meanings.note: Everyday clipped form of kilogramme; followed by de without an article: trois kilos de citrons.

examples.text: Il me faut deux kilos de pommes pour la compote.
examples.trans: I need two kilos of apples for the stewed fruit.

examples.text: Ce sac de farine pèse cinq kilos.
examples.trans: This bag of flour weighs five kilos.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le kilomètre', plural 'les kilomètres').

examples.text: La gare est à deux kilomètres d'ici, on y va à vélo?
examples.trans: The train station is two kilometers from here, shall we go by bike?

examples.text: Ma sœur court cinq kilomètres au parc tous les dimanches matin.
examples.trans: My sister runs five kilometers in the park every Sunday morning.

meanings.en: physiotherapist, physical therapist (colloquial short for kinésithérapeute)
meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le kiné', plural 'les kinés').

examples.text: J'ai rendez-vous chez le kiné à midi pour mon mal de dos.
examples.trans: I have an appointment with the physical therapist at noon for my backache.

examples.text: La kiné m'a montré trois exercices simples pour mon épaule.
examples.trans: The physical therapist showed me three simple exercises for my shoulder.

meanings.en: Koltès, a surname attested in eastern France, notably in the Lorraine region.
meanings.note: In French spelling, the grave accent on è indicates that the final syllable is pronounced [ɛs] with a sounded final s rather than a silent ending.

examples.text: J'emprunte un livre de Monsieur Koltès à la bibliothèque municipale.
examples.trans: I am borrowing a book by Mr. Koltès from the public library.

examples.text: Madame Koltès prend son petit déjeuner sur la terrasse du café.
examples.trans: Mrs. Koltès is having her breakfast on the café terrace.

meanings.en: UNICEF, the United Nations Children's Fund, preceded by the elided French definite article l'.
meanings.note: In French, organizational acronyms beginning with a pronounced vowel normally take the definite article with elision (l'UNICEF, l'ONU, l'UNESCO).

examples.text: Ma sœur fait un don mensuel à l'UNICEF.
examples.trans: My sister makes a monthly donation to UNICEF.

examples.text: J'ai acheté ces cartes de vœux au profit de l'UNICEF.
examples.trans: I bought these greeting cards in support of UNICEF.

examples.text: Après la mort de son vieux chat, notre voisine était très triste.
examples.trans: After the death of her old cat, our neighbor was very sad.

examples.text: Mon grand-père parle toujours de la vie et de la mort avec calme.
examples.trans: My grandfather always speaks calmly about life and death.

meanings.note: Scientific laboratory; in French bakeries and pastry shops, the back preparation kitchen.

examples.text: Bienvenue au laboratoire du gâteau du dimanche, les apprentis!
examples.trans: Welcome to the Sunday cake laboratory, apprentices!

examples.text: Le pâtissier prépare ses glaçages dès l'aube dans son laboratoire.
examples.trans: The pastry chef prepares his glazes at dawn in his workshop.

examples.text: En été, on adore se baigner dans l'eau fraîche du lac.
examples.trans: In summer, we love swimming in the cool water of the lake.

examples.text: Nous avons fait tout le tour du lac à pied après le déjeuner.
examples.trans: We walked all the way around the lake after lunch.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lacet', plural 'les lacets').

examples.text: Attention, ton lacet est défait, tu vas tomber dans l'escalier!
examples.trans: Watch out, your shoelace is untied, you're going to fall on the stairs!

examples.text: Le petit garçon apprend déjà à nouer ses lacets tout seul.
examples.trans: The little boy is already learning to tie his shoelaces all by himself.

meanings.note: En laine = made of wool.

examples.text: Et regardez, ce gilet doux en laine est propre et neuf. Essayez-le.
examples.trans: And look, this soft wool cardigan is clean and new. Try it on.

examples.text: Ma grand-mère tricote un bonnet en laine bien chaud pour l'hiver.
examples.trans: My grandmother is knitting a nice warm wool hat for winter.

meanings.note: laisser quelqu'un voir = to let someone see
Laisse-moi = let me.

examples.text: Laissez vos photos ici.
examples.trans: Leave your photos here.

examples.text: Laisse-moi parler!
examples.trans: Let me speak!

meanings.note: Du lait d'amande = almond milk.

examples.text: Un café au lait.
examples.trans: A coffee with milk.

examples.text: Peux-tu acheter une bouteille de lait frais en rentrant ce soir?
examples.trans: Can you buy a bottle of fresh milk on your way home tonight?

meanings.note: Built from lait ('milk').

examples.text: Le camion du laitier est en panne. Regardez dans le frigo!
examples.trans: The milkman's van has broken down. Look in the fridge!

examples.text: Autrefois, le laitier déposait des bouteilles en verre devant chaque porte.
examples.trans: In the old days, the milkman used to leave glass bottles in front of every door.

meanings.note: En laiton = made of brass.

examples.text: Oui, huit chambres, huit clés en laiton. Le client de la chambre quatre arrive aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: Yes, eight rooms, eight brass keys. Room four's guest arrives today.

examples.text: Il y a une lampe de lecture en laiton dans mon atelier en bas.
examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

examples.text: Branche la lampe en laiton d'Henri... oh, regarde cette belle lumière jaune!
examples.trans: Plug in Henri's brass lamp... oh, look at that lovely yellow light!

meanings.en: Lambert, a traditional French masculine given name and one of the most widespread French family names.
meanings.note: Popularized across northern Gaul and the Low Countries in the Middle Ages through the cult of Saint Lambert, 7th-century bishop of Maastricht.

examples.text: Monsieur Lambert répare son vélo devant le garage.
examples.trans: Mr. Lambert is repairing his bicycle in front of the garage.

examples.text: La pharmacie se trouve rue Lambert, près de la poste.
examples.trans: The pharmacy is on Lambert Street, near the post office.

lame.gloss: slat (of a shutter or floor); blade

meanings.en: wooden slat (of a louvered shutter or floorboard); blade
meanings.note: Covers thin flat strips of wood (*les lames d'un volet*, *les lames du parquet*) as well as knife blades.

examples.text: Peignez chaque petite lame du volet avec le pinceau fin.
examples.trans: Paint each little slat of the shutter with the thin brush.

examples.text: L'air passe doucement entre les lames des volets fermés.
examples.trans: Air passes gently between the slats of the closed shutters.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lampadaire', plural 'les lampadaires').

examples.text: Le lampadaire devant notre immeuble est cassé depuis trois jours.
examples.trans: The street lamp in front of our building has been broken for three days.

examples.text: Attendons-nous sous le lampadaire à la sortie du métro ce soir!
examples.trans: Let's wait for each other under the lamppost outside the subway tonight!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lampe', plural 'les lampes').

examples.text: Il m'a offert une jolie lampe.
examples.trans: He gave me a pretty lamp.

examples.text: Allume la petite lampe du salon, il commence à faire sombre.
examples.trans: Turn on the small living room lamp, it is starting to get dark.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to launch'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').
Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to throw'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').

meanings.en: se lancer: to take the plunge, embark on
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'se lancer: to take the plunge'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'lancé').

examples.text: Mon frère lance la balle au chien sur la pelouse.
examples.trans: My brother throws the ball to the dog on the lawn.

examples.text: Ma voisine va lancer une petite boutique de fleurs au printemps.
examples.trans: My neighbor is going to open a small flower shop in spring.

meanings.note: Le langage corporel. Masculine noun formed with the suffix '-age' (from Late Latin '-aticum') denoting an action, state, or collection. Standard masculine noun meaning 'language, speech'.

examples.text: Les jeunes utilisent parfois un langage que mes parents ne comprennent pas.
examples.trans: Young people sometimes use language that my parents don't understand.

examples.text: Même sans parler, son langage corporel montrait qu'il était fatigué.
examples.trans: Even without speaking, his body language showed that he was tired.

meanings.note: Hanging courtyard or street lantern.

examples.text: Henri, est-ce que tu accroches ces lanternes en papier pour midi?
examples.trans: Henri, are you hanging those paper lanterns for noon?

examples.text: Regardez ces lanternes dorées sous le ciel du soir, comme c'est paisible!
examples.trans: Look at those golden lanterns against the evening sky, how peaceful!

meanings.en: Lanvin, a French family name also well known internationally through Parisian fashion history.
meanings.note: Contains two French nasal vowels in sequence: [ɑ̃] followed by [ɛ̃].

examples.text: Madame Lanvin choisit une écharpe en laine dans la boutique.
examples.trans: Mrs. Lanvin is choosing a wool scarf in the shop.

examples.text: Le facteur apporte un colis pour Monsieur Lanvin.
examples.trans: The mail carrier is bringing a parcel for Mr. Lanvin.

examples.text: Les enfants ont donné une carotte fraîche au petit lapin blanc.
examples.trans: The children gave a fresh carrot to the little white rabbit.

examples.text: On a aperçu un lapin sauvage au fond du pré ce matin.
examples.trans: We spotted a wild rabbit at the back of the meadow this morning.

meanings.note: False friend: means 'wide', not 'large' (grand).

examples.text: Attention, Étienne, le bec de la carafe est large!
examples.trans: Careful, Etienne, the pitcher spout is wide!

examples.text: Cet endroit est vraiment large.
examples.trans: This place is really wide, broad.

meanings.note: largement suffisant = more than enough

examples.text: Ne cours pas, on a largement le temps d'attraper notre train!
examples.trans: Don't run, we have plenty of time to catch our train!

examples.text: Deux grandes pizzas suffiront largement pour nous quatre ce soir.
examples.trans: Two large pizzas will be more than enough for the four of us tonight.

meanings.note: Built from large ('wide').

examples.text: Regardez les mots à côté du nôtre: Largeur de cour, bruit de rue, note de calme, neuf sur dix!
examples.trans: Look at the words beside ours: Courtyard width, street noise, quiet score, nine out of ten!

examples.text: Mesure bien la largeur de la porte avant d'acheter ce canapé!
examples.trans: Measure the width of the door carefully before buying that sofa!

meanings.en: to dump, drop (a romantic partner); to ditch
meanings.note: Informal/familiar. Regular -er verb; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'largué').
Regular -er verb; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'largué').

examples.text: Son petit ami l'a larguée par message hier soir, c'est terrible.
examples.trans: Her boyfriend dumped her by text last night, it's awful.

examples.text: Il a fini par larguer ses vieux meubles avant de déménager à Paris.
examples.trans: He ended up getting rid of his old furniture before moving to Paris.

meanings.note: Avoir les larmes aux yeux = have tears in one's eyes.

examples.text: En écoutant le violon, il avait les larmes aux yeux.
examples.trans: Listening to the violin, he had tears in his eyes.

examples.text: Couper des oignons fait toujours venir les larmes.
examples.trans: Chopping onions always brings tears.

meanings.note: Rayon laser. Masculine noun ('le laser', plural 'les lasers').
Jouer au laser. Masculine noun ('le laser', plural 'les lasers').

examples.text: L'ophtalmologue a soigné son œil grâce à un traitement au laser.
examples.trans: The eye doctor treated his eye using a laser treatment.

examples.text: Mon chat devient fou dès qu'il voit le point rouge d'un laser!
examples.trans: My cat goes crazy as soon as he sees the red dot of a laser!

meanings.note: Jouer au laser game. Spoken French phrase expression meaning 'laser tag game', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Pour son anniversaire, mon fils veut faire un laser game avec ses copains.
examples.trans: For his birthday, my son wants to play laser tag with his buddies.

examples.text: On a bien rigolé au laser game samedi après-midi malgré la fatigue!
examples.trans: We had a great laugh playing laser tag on Saturday afternoon despite being tired!

meanings.note: Narrow wooden slat of a park bench, crate, or bed frame.

examples.text: Les lattes du banc viennent d'être repeintes en vert sombre.
examples.trans: The slats of the bench have just been repainted dark green.

examples.text: Une inscription discrète se cache sous la troisième latte.
examples.trans: A discreet inscription hides beneath the third slat.

meanings.en: Laura, a feminine given name widely used in French and across European languages.
meanings.note: While Laure is the inherited French vernacular form, Laura became extremely popular in France in the late 20th century alongside international forms.

examples.text: Laura prépare une salade de fruits dans la cuisine.
examples.trans: Laura is making a fruit salad in the kitchen.

examples.text: Tu peux appeler Laura avant le dîner, s'il te plaît?
examples.trans: Can you call Laura before dinner, please?

meanings.en: Laure, a traditional French feminine given name equivalent to English Laura.
meanings.note: Also frequently combined in French hyphenated given names such as Anne-Laure and Marie-Laure.

examples.text: Laure travaille à la mairie du lundi au vendredi.
examples.trans: Laure works at town hall from Monday to Friday.

examples.text: Nous allons déjeuner chez Laure dimanche midi.
examples.trans: We are going to have lunch at Laure's place at noon on Sunday.

meanings.en: Laurence, a French feminine given name corresponding to English Lauren or feminine Laurence.
meanings.note: Notice the false-friend gender contrast with English: in modern French, Laurence is overwhelmingly feminine, whereas the masculine counterpart is Laurent.

examples.text: Laurence prend le métro tous les matins à huit heures.
examples.trans: Laurence takes the subway every morning at eight o'clock.

examples.text: Peux-tu prêter ton parapluie à Laurence?
examples.trans: Can you lend your umbrella to Laurence?

meanings.note: Able to be washed off with water ('encre lavable' = washable ink).

examples.text: Heureusement pour nos manches, cette encre bleue est lavable à l'eau!
examples.trans: Luckily for our sleeves, this blue ink is washable in water!

examples.text: Nous utilisons des nappes en lin facilement lavables.
examples.trans: We use easily washable linen tablecloths.

meanings.en: to wash (windows, dishes, clothes, or hands)
meanings.note: Transitive for objects (laver les vitres); reflexive when washing oneself or part of the body (se laver les mains).

examples.text: Nous allons laver toutes les grandes vitres avant vendredi.
examples.trans: We are going to wash all the tall windowpanes before Friday.

examples.text: Claire lave soigneusement les douze tasses neuves.
examples.trans: Claire carefully washes the twelve new cups.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel
As a direct-object pronoun: le is masculine, la feminine; both become l' before a vowel sound.

examples.text: Le film est fantastique.
examples.trans: The film is fantastic.

examples.text: Le pain frais du matin sent tellement bon dans toute la cuisine!
examples.trans: Fresh morning bread smells so good throughout the whole kitchen!

meanings.note: As a noun naming the colour, masculine; as an adjective, feminine verte.

examples.text: Ma sœur adore le vert, surtout pour ses pulls de printemps.
examples.trans: My sister loves green, especially for her spring sweaters.

examples.text: Pour repeindre les volets de la maison, je préfère le vert au bleu.
examples.trans: For repainting the house shutters, I prefer green over blue.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la lecture', plural 'les lectures').

examples.text: Il y a une lampe de lecture en laiton dans mon atelier en bas.
examples.trans: There is a brass reading lamp in my workshop downstairs.

examples.text: Le soir, la lecture au salon est très calme.
examples.trans: In the evening, reading in the lounge is very calm.

meanings.en: Lecœur, a French surname literally meaning 'the heart'.
meanings.note: Written traditionally with the œ ligature (Lecœur), though civil-registry records without typographic ligatures also spell it Lecoeur.

examples.text: Monsieur Lecœur cultive des tomates dans son jardin.
examples.trans: Mr. Lecœur grows tomatoes in his garden.

examples.text: Vous avez un rendez-vous chez le docteur Lecœur demain matin.
examples.trans: You have an appointment with Dr. Lecœur tomorrow morning.

meanings.en: Lelouch, a surname of Maghrebi (Algerian and Tunisian) origin widely attested in France.
meanings.note: Related orthographic variants in French civil registries include Lellouche, Lellouch, and Allouche.

examples.text: Monsieur Lelouch gare sa voiture devant la mairie.
examples.trans: Mr. Lelouch parks his car in front of town hall.

examples.text: Nous avons croisé Madame Lelouch au marché ce matin.
examples.trans: We ran into Mrs. Lelouch at the market this morning.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le lendemain', plural 'les lendemains').

examples.text: On est arrivés très tard et on a dormi jusqu'à midi le lendemain.
examples.trans: We arrived very late and slept until noon the next day.

examples.text: Ce plat en sauce est encore meilleur réchauffé le lendemain!
examples.trans: This stew is even better reheated the next day!

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'slow'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Le rythme du film est un peu lent.
examples.trans: The pace of the movie is a bit slow.

examples.text: La circulation en ville à midi est toujours lente.
examples.trans: City traffic at noon is always slow.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a . mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Parlez plus lentement, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Speak more slowly, please.

examples.text: Toujours là pour t'entendre jouer ta gamme de fa majeur lentement, Thibault!
examples.trans: Still here waiting to hear you play your F-major scale slowly, Thibault!

meanings.note: Named from Latin *lenticula*; optical glass lenses were later named after the biconvex shape of a lentil!

examples.text: Une soupe chaude de lentilles dorées réchauffe tout l'hiver.
examples.trans: A hot soup of golden lentils warms you up all winter.

examples.text: Les lentilles cuisent vite avec une carotte et un peu de thym.
examples.trans: Lentils cook quickly with a carrot and a bit of thyme.

meanings.en: Leprince, a common French surname literally meaning 'the prince'.
meanings.note: Belongs to the widespread French class of status-title nicknames alongside Leroi ('the king'), Leduc ('the duke'), and Lecomte ('the count').

examples.text: Madame Leprince enseigne les mathématiques au lycée.
examples.trans: Mrs. Leprince teaches mathematics at the high school.

examples.text: La clé de l'appartement est chez Monsieur Leprince.
examples.trans: The key to the apartment is at Mr. Leprince's place.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and number with the noun it replaces

examples.text: Il doit y avoir une solution! — Laquelle?
examples.trans: There must be a solution! — Which one?

examples.text: Lequel tu préfères?
examples.trans: Which one do you prefer?

examples.text: Laquelle? On pourrait dire qu'il y a une nouvelle taxe sur les acteurs français?
examples.trans: Which one? Could we say there's a new tax on French actors?

meanings.note: une note de frais = an expense claim
De l'eau fraîche.

examples.text: On partage les frais d'essence et de péage pour descendre à Bordeaux?
examples.trans: Shall we split the gas and toll expenses for driving down to Bordeaux?

examples.text: Mon entreprise rembourse tous les frais de transport pour ce déplacement.
examples.trans: My company reimburses all travel expenses for this business trip.

meanings.note: Descriptive French adjective meaning 'washed out'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Après huit heures de déménagement dans les escaliers, je suis complètement lessivé!
examples.trans: After eight hours of moving boxes up and down the stairs, I'm completely wiped out!

examples.text: Ma mère est rentrée lessivée de sa longue garde à l'hôpital.
examples.trans: My mother came home exhausted from her long shift at the hospital.

meanings.note: Envoyer une lettre.

examples.text: Le facteur dépose une lettre importante dans ma boîte aux lettres.
examples.trans: The mailman drops an important letter in my mailbox.

examples.text: J'écris une longue lettre à ma grand-mère chaque mois.
examples.trans: I write a long letter to my grandmother every month.

meanings.note: Leurs before a plural noun.

examples.text: Mes voisins promènent leur petit chien tous les matins au parc.
examples.trans: My neighbors walk their little dog every morning in the park.

examples.text: Les clients boivent leur café chaud sur la terrasse ensoleillée.
examples.trans: The customers drink their hot coffee on the sunny patio.

meanings.en: to raise, lift (se lever = to get up, stand up)
meanings.note: Regular -er verb; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'levé').

examples.text: Grand, manteau gris foncé, il lève les yeux vers l'enseigne de notre hôtel!
examples.trans: Tall, dark grey coat, he is looking up at our hotel sign!

examples.text: lève les yeux
examples.trans: looks up

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le levier', plural 'les leviers').

examples.text: Tire doucement ce petit levier vers le bas pour ouvrir le capot.
examples.trans: Gently pull this little lever down to open the hood.

examples.text: Le mécanicien a réparé le levier de vitesse de ma vieille voiture.
examples.trans: The mechanic repaired the gearshift lever on my old car.

meanings.en: lesson, educational instruction or piece of advice
meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la leçon', plural 'les leçons').

examples.text: Mon frère prend sa première leçon de guitare mercredi prochain.
examples.trans: My brother is taking his first guitar lesson next Wednesday.

examples.text: J'ai oublié mon parapluie sous l'averse: ça me servira de leçon!
examples.trans: I forgot my umbrella in the downpour: that will teach me a lesson!

meanings.en: Li, a very common Chinese family name (and occasional given-name syllable) used in French without tonal diacritics.
meanings.note: Lǐ (李) is one of the most populous family names in the world and is invariable in French grammar.

examples.text: Monsieur Li ouvre son restaurant à onze heures trente.
examples.trans: Mr. Li opens his restaurant at eleven thirty.

examples.text: J'étudie à l'université dans le même groupe que Madame Li.
examples.trans: I study at the university in the same group as Mrs. Li.

meanings.note: Liberté conditionnelle = parole.

examples.text: En vacances au camping, les enfants adorent ce sentiment de liberté.
examples.trans: On vacation at the campsite, the kids love that feeling of freedom.

examples.text: Travailler depuis la maison me donne beaucoup plus de liberté le matin.
examples.trans: Working from home gives me a lot more freedom in the morning.

meanings.note: Same form in masculine and feminine: le libraire / la libraire (false friend: librarian is bibliothécaire).

examples.text: La libraire d'à côté nous apporte souvent le courrier.
examples.trans: The bookshop owner next door often brings us the mail.

examples.text: Demandez conseil à la libraire du quartier.
examples.trans: Ask the neighborhood bookseller for advice.

meanings.note: Shop that sells books (false friend: a lending library is 'une bibliothèque').

examples.text: J'adore flâner dans la petite librairie du coin.
examples.trans: I love browsing in the little corner bookshop.

examples.text: La vitrine de la librairie présente des romans de voyage.
examples.trans: The bookshop window displays travel novels.

meanings.note: Available for an appointment or work.
At liberty; free of charge is gratuit, a different meaning.

examples.text: Elle est libre dans trois semaines.
examples.trans: She's free in three weeks.

examples.text: Henri... Claire... dites-moi que la chambre six est libre ce soir, s'il vous plaît.
examples.trans: Henri... Claire... please tell me room six is free tonight.

meanings.note: Manner adverb formed by adding '-ment' (from Latin 'mente', 'with a . mind') to the feminine adjective stem.

examples.text: Chez nous, chacun peut donner son avis librement autour de la table.
examples.trans: In our home, everyone can share their opinion freely around the table.

examples.text: Les chevaux courent librement dans le grand pré derrière la ferme.
examples.trans: The horses run freely in the big meadow behind the farm.

meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'to free'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'libéré').

meanings.en: se libérer: to free oneself, break free, let oneself go
meanings.note: Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin '-are') meaning 'se liberer: to free oneself'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'libéré').

examples.text: Peux-tu te libérer une heure à midi pour déjeuner avec moi?
examples.trans: Can you free yourself up for an hour at noon to have lunch with me?

examples.text: Les clients du fond partent, ils vont bientôt libérer la table.
examples.trans: The customers in the back are leaving, they will free up the table soon.

meanings.note: lier deux personnes = to bind two people together

examples.text: Ce qui nous lie vraiment.
examples.trans: What truly binds us.

examples.text: Une grande amitié lie nos deux familles depuis plus de vingt ans.
examples.trans: A deep friendship has connected our two families for over twenty years.

meanings.note: Masculine noun (*du lierre grimpant*). Historically *l'ierre* (from Latin *hedera*) fused its definite article into the word itself!

examples.text: Le lierre vert grimpe autour de la vieille grille en fer.
examples.trans: Green ivy climbs around the old iron gate.

examples.text: Écartez doucement le lierre avant de repeindre le mur.
examples.trans: Gently move the ivy aside before repainting the wall.

meanings.note: In au lieu de, literally in the place of, it forms the expression instead of.

examples.text: Deux cachets au lieu d'un.
examples.trans: Two fees instead of one.

examples.text: Cette petite place ombragée est un lieu très calme pour lire.
examples.trans: This shady little square is a very quiet place to read.

meanings.note: Cosmetic surgery to tighten facial skin.

examples.text: Elles ont toutes le même lifting.
examples.trans: They all have the same facelift.

examples.text: Pas de lifting pour moi!
examples.trans: No facelift for me!

examples.text: Une ligne droite.
examples.trans: A straight line.

examples.text: La ligne est occupée.
examples.trans: The line is busy.

examples.text: Imaginez qu'il y a une ligne invisible entre nous.
examples.trans: Imagine there's an invisible line between us.

meanings.note: Il y a des limites. Feminine noun ('la limite', plural 'les limites').

examples.text: La limite de vitesse est de trente kilomètres à l'heure devant l'école.
examples.trans: The speed limit is thirty kilometers per hour in front of the school.

examples.text: Ma patience a des limites quand le voisin fait du bruit à minuit!
examples.trans: My patience has limits when the neighbor makes noise at midnight!

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la limousine', plural 'les limousines').

examples.text: Les jeunes mariés sont arrivés devant la mairie dans une longue limousine blanche.
examples.trans: The newlyweds arrived in front of town hall in a long white limousine.

examples.text: Les enfants ont regardé passer la limousine avec de grands yeux surpris.
examples.trans: The children watched the limousine drive by with wide, surprised eyes.

meanings.note: Perfectly clear and transparent (of water, sky, or an explanation).

examples.text: En voyant ces anneaux, la note du cartographe devient limpide!
examples.trans: Seeing these rings, the mapmaker's note becomes crystal clear!

examples.text: L'eau de la fontaine est fraîche et limpide.
examples.trans: The fountain water is cool and crystal clear.

meanings.note: Flax plant or crisp woven linen fabric and thread ('fil de lin', 'nappe en lin').

examples.text: Les tables sont dressées avec des nappes en lin écru.
examples.trans: The tables are set with unbleached linen tablecloths.

examples.text: Le carnet ancien est relié avec un fil de lin solide.
examples.trans: The old notebook is bound with strong linen thread.

meanings.en: Linda, a feminine given name used in French and many other languages.
meanings.note: In French, the sequence in before a vowel or in this borrowed name is commonly pronounced [in] ([linda]) rather than nasalized [ɛ̃], though [lɛ̃da] also occurs regionally.

examples.text: Linda boit un thé chaud dans le salon.
examples.trans: Linda is drinking hot tea in the living room.

examples.text: Nous partons en vacances à la montagne avec Linda.
examples.trans: We are going on vacation to the mountains with Linda.

examples.text: On prend un cours de Lindy Hop.
examples.trans: We are taking a Lindy Hop class.

examples.text: Elle adore danser le Lindy.
examples.trans: She loves dancing the Lindy.

meanings.en: Line, a French feminine given name originating as a short form of names ending in -line.
meanings.note: Used both as an independent legal given name in France and in compound names such as Marie-Line or Anne-Line.

examples.text: Line arrose les fleurs sur son balcon chaque soir.
examples.trans: Line waters the flowers on her balcony every evening.

examples.text: J'ai acheté une boîte de chocolats pour l'anniversaire de Line.
examples.trans: I bought a box of chocolates for Line's birthday.

meanings.note: Armoire à linge = linen cupboard.

examples.text: J'apporte des draps blancs propres de l'armoire à linge!
examples.trans: I will bring clean white sheets from the linen cupboard!

examples.text: Il fait beau aujourd'hui, je vais étendre le linge dehors au soleil.
examples.trans: The weather is nice today, I'm going to hang the laundry outside in the sun.

meanings.note: Fort comme un lion.

examples.text: Les enfants ont attendu longtemps pour voir le lion dormir au zoo.
